receipts.first_text_witness: Last month, I opened my banking app and tapped the one screen nobody ever taps, interest earned year-to-date, $1.04. I had about 10 grand sitting in that account all year, and my bank paid me a dollar four. Meanwhile, that same bank, in a single recent year, made 92.6 billion dollars off the gap between what it pays people like me and what it charges people like me. And here's the part that actually got under my skin. Everything I'm about to show you today was sitting in plain sight the whole time, on government
receipts.last_text_witness: box, swapping a fund, and opening an HSA, four settings the system preset against you and quietly hoped you'd never inspect. The financial industry's entire business model is the assumption that you won't do boring paperwork. Tonight, be the rounding error in their forecast because nobody hands out trophies for working seven extra years to fund someone else's record quarter. If this opened your eyes even a little, share it with the person you know who still banks where they did at 19. I'll see you in the next one.

receipts.mobile_transform: Native 480×360 retained. Proportional 320×240 view; 320×180 canvas fits a proportional 240×180 image with black sidebars, without cropping or stretching.

primary_source_receipts.finding: 2024 NII of $92.583 billion rounds to $92.6 billion; net income is a separate $58.5 billion measure.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Group NII includes investments, wholesale and credit activity. The personal anecdote and attribution to retail inertia are unverified.

primary_source_receipts.finding: The author specifies zero starting net worth, 5% real accumulation returns and 4% withdrawals with flexible spending.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Deterministic educational model, not a retirement-date guarantee; pensions and benefits are separate funding sources.

primary_source_receipts.finding: $250,000 coverage per depositor, insured bank and ownership category; same-category deposits aggregate.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Deposit coverage is not investment-loss insurance or proof of historical product rates.

primary_source_receipts.finding: The producer Chase rate-sheet search extract includes a 0.01% standard rate.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Exact June 7 rates for all named products/geographies and a specific 4% competitor remain unverified. Mutable current sheets cannot establish upload-era terms.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Promised match mean 4.6%, median 4%; median deferral needed 6%, mean 6.5%.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Vanguard plan sample and promised formula, not universal employer terms or vested market return. Exact most-common formula was not authenticated from the returned extract.

primary_source_receipts.finding: The producer release extract identifies $1,336 annual missed match and the $24 billion headline.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Direct PDF access failed. Full sample and income-group tables were not read from the producer; exact 4.4M/25%/42%/10% claims remain unverified and are not 2026 statistics.

primary_source_receipts.finding: 78.78% of active large-cap funds underperformed in 2025. All 18 domestic and four international equity categories show majority 15-year underperformance.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Twenty-two categories are not US-only. Aggregated overlapping categories do not establish a universal manager-loss probability or identical portfolio exposure.

primary_source_receipts.finding: 0.40% is the asset-weighted ratio for all equity mutual funds, with 0.05% for index equity; active domestic equity averages 0.64%.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Fund universe and weights matter; labeling 0.40% as active alone is incorrect. These are not matched individual investment outcomes.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Plan administration and investment expenses can include loads, redemption, surrender and transfer charges.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: A low-expense all-stock fund can change risk. No universal five-to-seven working-year cost per 1% fee is established.

primary_source_receipts.finding: 2026 limits are $4,400 self-only and $8,750 family; HDHP deductible minimums $1,700/$3,400 and out-of-pocket maximums $8,500/$17,000.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Employer funding and monthly eligibility count. Limits do not supply free contributed capital or universal eligibility.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Eligibility includes coverage, other-coverage, Medicare and dependent rules. Qualified medical distributions are federally tax-free; nonmedical amounts can be taxable plus 20% before age 65.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Not every policy/person qualifies. Premium exceptions are limited; state rules, investment losses, fees and healthcare timing matter.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Section 125 HSA salary reduction is excluded from employment tax; ordinary employee payroll deductions are wages.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Full 7.65% marginal benefit is not universal across wage bases and payroll arrangements.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Q39 permits delayed reimbursement without a time limit for qualified post-establishment expenses, with records and no duplicate reimbursement or deduction.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: A receipt supports its eligible expense amount, not tax-free withdrawal of every investment gain.

primary_source_receipts.finding: The producer’s 2025 estimate is $172,500 per retiring 65-year-old; twice this is $345,000.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: An actuarial estimate with Medicare assumptions and exclusions, not a guaranteed future household bill or complete early-retirement budget.

primary_source_receipts.finding: The 2025 PSCA sponsor-survey announcement reports 20% of participants investing, up from 18%.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Sample-specific participant rate, not national asset share. Cash can be needed for near-term medical expenses.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Median household money income was $83,730 in 2024.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Not exactly 2026 salary or take-home; household composition, tax and benefit circumstances vary.

primary_source_receipts.finding: 2026 employee 401(k) limit $24,500 and base IRA limit $7,500. Roth phaseouts $153K–$168K single and $242K–$252K joint.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: IRA limits apply per eligible person with compensation; HSA eligibility is separate. A household may have more than one eligible IRA.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Conversions can be taxable. Separate five-tax-year recapture clocks and contribution/conversion/earnings ordering apply.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Seasoned conversion principal is distinct from qualified earnings. Low conversion tax and healthcare-credit effects need household inputs.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Continue payments until the later of five years or age 59½; prohibited modification can cause recapture.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Account and formula restrictions apply. A penalty exception does not eliminate ordinary income tax.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Separation in or after the year of turning 55 can qualify for employer-plan early-penalty relief, not IRA relief.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Plan payment terms and ordinary tax remain. A rollover to IRA removes this particular exception.

primary_source_receipts.finding: The March 18, 2026 producer release reports vacatur of the 2024 rule and restoration of the ERISA five-part test.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Direct page returned 403; search abstract only. This does not repeal SEC Reg BI or investment-adviser fiduciary duties.

primary_source_receipts.finding: The 2019 SEC interpretation describes investment-adviser fiduciary care and loyalty.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Service and relationship scope matter; a separate DOL vacatur does not make all retail advice suitability-only.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Broker recommendations of securities or strategies to retail customers fall under Regulation Best Interest.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: Application depends on recommendation and capacity; self-directed execution alone differs.

primary_source_receipts.finding: BCG estimates $128 trillion global AUM at end-2024.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: The exact $144T claim is not authenticated; differing universes and endpoints are not interchangeable. AUM is not revenue.

primary_source_receipts.finding: Producer search material identifies a 3.9% 2025 base for 30 years and 90% success; 2024 base was 3.7%.
primary_source_receipts.limitations: The full PDF was identified but not read. Exact 4.7% primary research was not inspected. Methods and horizons differ; no perpetual guarantee.

calculation_receipts.assumptions_and_limits: Same channel, format and snapshot; age at least seven days; peers at 0.5–2× target age; sort absolute age difference then ID. Thresholds 2 and 0.5 unchanged. Lifetime rates are historical, not current velocity or causal evidence.

Zero starting assets, constant real income/spending, end-year deposits, no benefits; taxes and fees must be absorbed in the assumed net real return. This is neither a backtest nor a success-probability simulation.
Stable APYs and balance for a full year; no fees, before personal tax and inflation. Creator’s $1.04 is not independently verified. The increment is $399.
Illustrative plan formula, not universal terms. Eligibility, vesting, access, taxes and market losses qualify the matching credit. $43K needs an explicit return and deposit convention.
Annual return minus fee, no new contributions, taxes or return variation. $558,314/$324,340 differ from the stated $574K/$334K. The stored $8.24M amount is an unverified ASR discrepancy.
Annual return minus fee, no new contributions or tax. Service benefits or differential investment outcomes are not modeled; there is no universal conversion to working years.
Constant nominal $8,750 end-year deposits, 7% return, no fees or withdrawals, and continuous eligibility. Future limits/returns may change. A 3% inflation case is illustrative, not a forecast.
Full 7.65% employee marginal FICA and eligible Section 125 payroll assumed. Not ordinary payroll deduction or all wage levels; the benefit is not free $8,750 principal.
Take-home after new deferrals is undefined. Employee versus employer money and gross versus net denominators must remain separate. Tax savings do not remove the need to fund higher contributions.

The stated story saves six to seven years. The cited zero-start 9% model differs from the claimed 33 years. Bridge estimates use two expense interpretations; neither is an authenticated funded account.
Same underlying allocation/return assumed. 0.50%→0.05% is a 0.45-percentage-point cost reduction. The working-year benefit is model-specific, not a promise.
Illustrative withdrawal rates and inflation, not recommendations or guarantees. Taxes, healthcare, longevity, sequence risk and access require a household model.
Six years × 250 workdays gives 1,500 one-way commute occasions; six × 52 gives 312 Sundays. Rounding and employment patterns vary. Health estimate doubling is arithmetic, not a future guarantee.

limits: Producer search extracts are not full-text receipts. Exact historical bank rates, match-study tables, $144T source, universal five-to-seven-year rule and 4.7% primary study remain unverified. No audio, video-frame or native Excel verification.
